verified.exploit_entry_point: A real HTTP S3 client. `rclone serve s3 --auth-proxy <prog>` is started (no --auth-key) on localhost; the auth proxy maps access key IDs to backends. A client signs an AWS SigV4 request for a proxy-known access key ID (alice/bob) with an EMPTY secret and sends it over HTTP. On the vulnerable code the server registers the client-presented access key ID in gofakes3 with an empty secret (authPairMiddleware) and gofakes3 verifies the SigV4 signature against that empty secret, so the empty-secret signature matches and the request is served as that identity. Confirmed against the built binary: list buckets (200), GET object returns the victim's file content (200), PUT (200), DELETE (204) - all for an access key ID whose real secret the attacker never knew.
variants: GET service (list buckets) as alice with empty secret - the reported path.
GET object as alice with empty secret - reads the victim's object content (data disclosure).
PUT object as alice with empty secret - writes into the victim's bucket.
DELETE object as alice with empty secret - deletes the victim's object.
GET service as a DIFFERENT proxy-mapped identity (bob) with empty secret - proves the flaw is not tied to one access key ID or backend.
verified.variant_coverage_note: The candidate marked this single-site (S1=no): all operations pass through one auth gate, so the task's hardness is S2 (the signature check that 'passes' is in gofakes3, but the bad state - an empty secret registered for the client-chosen key - is created earlier by the middleware) and S7 (an over-broad fix breaks legitimate proxy-only use). The variants span list/get/put/delete and two distinct backends so a fix must stop the whole class, not one request.
services: none (the auth proxy is a local helper program; the S3 server and the test client both run on localhost, no real remote)
verified.project_tests_run: rclone's own serve s3 tests (cmd/serve/s3/s3_test.go) require a minio docker backend and/or in-process harness and were not run as-is. Instead the behaviour was verified end to end against the compiled `rclone serve s3` binary at both the vulnerable parent and the fix commit using an out-of-tree HTTP client harness (the task's own tests), mirroring the fix commit's own added regression tests TestAuthProxyEmptySecret / TestAuthProxyKeysNotRegistered. Vulnerable binary: 0/5 security (all attacks succeed), 5/5 functional. Fix commit and the source-only reference patch: 5/5 security, 5/5 functional, reward 1.0 (run twice, identical).

patch_checks._why: 2026-10-16: a fix that refuses every --auth-proxy request scored 1.0 in rclone-sib (same commit); TestS3Proxy*CorrectSecretServed must now fail it.
2026-10-16: reference fix plus refusing every non-GET/HEAD request in --auth-proxy mode (verifies reads, refuses writes). TestS3ProxyAliceCorrectSecretPut/DeleteServed must fail it.

notes: Go 1.26. The reference fix.patch is the upstream commit reduced to the three behavioural source files (cmd/serve/proxy/proxy.go, cmd/serve/s3/s3.go, cmd/serve/s3/server.go); the upstream test files, docs and the build-ignored proxy_code.go test helpers are dropped. gofakes3 v0.0.9 (which has V4SignVerifyWithSecret) is already pinned at the vulnerable parent commit, so the fix needs no dependency bump. The rclone binary is pre-built into the image with the Go module/build caches baked in; the verifier rebuilds only the packages the solver changed, offline. See notes.md for the inherent cross-version limitation on positive proxy tests.
_leak_terms_note: 2026-10-16: _secret_access_key removed from leak_terms. It is the proxy's interface (where the secret is returned), which a correct fix cannot discover: it is documented only in the upstream fix. The tests need it, so the instruction states it; where and how to verify is still left to the solver.
